## Arrhenius rate constants and their temperature bands (`type: arrhenius`) {#sec-ch06-arrhenius}

### Summary

Most gas-phase reactions take their rate constant from the modified Arrhenius law: a pre-exponential factor, a power
of temperature and an activation term. kintera also accepts several temperature bands per reaction, each with its
own parameters, so that tabulated rate data with different fits in different temperature ranges can be used as
given.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $k = A (T/T_{\mathrm{ref}})^{b} \exp(-E_a/T)$ per band, @eq-ch06-arrhenius-rate.

**Data.** $T$ [K] in; $k$ in mol, m, s units out; YAML $A$ in molecule, cm, s units.

**Placement.** First evaluator of `Kinetics.forward`.

**Activation.** `type: arrhenius`; keys `A`[^rg-9b44b7a77056], `b`[^rg-b2b59650290c], `Ea_R`[^rg-3a030b87ff19], `E4`, `A_ranges`, `T_ranges`, `b_ranges`, `Ea_R_ranges`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact; inactive bands are never evaluated.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $A$, pre-exponential factor (units set by the reaction order); $b$, temperature exponent [-];
$E_a$, activation temperature [K] (the YAML key `Ea_R`, an energy divided by $\mathcal R$); $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$,
reference temperature [K] (default 300 K).

Defaults when a key is omitted: `A` is 1, `b` is 0, `Ea_R` is 1 K, `E4` is 0. The `Ea_R` default of 1 K, not 0, is a
verified finding: options read from a card with no `Ea_R` report `Ea_R() == [1.0]`, so the rate constant carries a
factor $\exp(-1/T)$, about 0.99 at 100 K. Whether this default is intended is an open question.

### Derivation

Within one temperature band the rate constant is

$$
k_j(T) = A_j \left(\frac{T}{T_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right)^{b_j} \exp\!\left(-\frac{E_{a,j}}{T}\right) .
$$ {#eq-ch06-arrhenius-rate}

The YAML value of $A$ is given in molecule, cm, s units. For a reaction whose reactant coefficients sum to $n$,
$A$ carries $\mathrm{molecule}^{1-n}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3(1-n)}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and the reader converts it to mol, m, s
units before it is stored. @eq-ch06-arrhenius-rate is computed in `forward`
({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::forward >}}); the unit conversion happens in `from_yaml`
({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

With bands, band $r$ of reaction $j$ covers $[T_{r-1}, T_r)$; the first band extends to 0 K and the last to
$+\infty$, so every temperature falls in exactly one band. The full derivation of the unit factor is not drafted
yet.

### Numerical method

`reset` ({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::reset >}}) pads the band tables to a common number of
bands; padded slots have $A = 0$ and an empty window. With one band, `forward` evaluates
@eq-ch06-arrhenius-rate directly. With several, it first selects the active band's $A$, $b$ and $E_a$ by a mask
on $T$ and only then evaluates the exponential, so an inactive band far outside its range cannot overflow. The
result is passed through the pressure switch of @sec-ch06-pressure-switch.

**Adding a rate-constant form: the evaluator contract.** A new form is C++ code compiled into kintera; at the pin there
is no way to register an evaluator at run time or from Python. The contract below is read from the code at the pin;
the Arrhenius evaluator is the model to copy.

*Classes to add.* (a) An options struct `XOptionsImpl` with its `std::shared_ptr` alias, holding one entry per
reaction in `ADD_ARG` fields, a `reactions()` list of `Reaction` objects and a static `from_yaml` that reads the
`reactions` list and keeps the entries of its own `type`[^rg-36105a006e4f], converting the pre-exponential factor from molecule, cm, s
units with `UnitSystem::convert_from` (@sec-ch02-units), as
{{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} does. (b) A module
`XImpl : torch::nn::Cloneable<XImpl>` with `TORCH_MODULE(X)`, whose constructor stores the options and calls `reset`,
and whose `reset` turns the per-reaction parameters into tensors registered with `register_buffer`
({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.hpp ArrheniusImpl >}}, {{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::reset >}}).

*The callback.* The module must have exactly the signature the evaluator list calls,

```cpp
torch::Tensor forward(torch::Tensor T, torch::Tensor P, torch::Tensor C,
                      std::map<std::string, torch::Tensor> const& other);
```

because `KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}) stores every evaluator as a
`torch::nn::AnyModule` and calls `forward(T, P, C, other)` on it. With `...` the batch shape of the caller's temperature
(for example `(ncol, nlyr)`) and $n$ the number of reactions of this evaluator, the arguments are:

| argument | shape | units | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `T` | `(...)`; `(..., n)` with `evolve_temperature` | K | the caller's temperature; with `evolve_temperature`, a view of it expanded to one column per reaction with gradient tracking on |
| `P` | `(...)` | Pa | the caller's pressure, passed through unchanged |
| `C` | `(..., nspecies, n)` | mol m$^{-3}$ | the caller's concentrations expanded to one column per reaction, cloned, with gradient tracking on; species in the kinetics order, gases first, then condensates |
| `other` | map | | the caller's extra tensors (for example `number_density`, `kf_override`), plus `gas_mask`, shape `(nspecies,)`, true for the gases, and `stoich`, shape `(nspecies, n)`, this evaluator's columns of the net stoichiometry |
| return | `(..., n)` | mol, m, s | the rate constant $k_r$ of each reaction, not the rate: `Kinetics` multiplies by the mass-action product afterwards (@sec-ch06-mass-action) |

: Arguments and return value of a rate-constant evaluator's `forward`, as `Kinetics` calls it. {#tbl-ch06-arrhenius-evaluator}

The returned tensor is copied into the evaluator's columns of one result tensor allocated with the shape, dtype and
device of `T` plus a reaction axis, so it must broadcast to `(..., n)`, and `Kinetics` keeps no reference to it.

*Derivatives.* After the call, `Kinetics` runs one backward pass of $\sum_r k_r$ and reads
$\partial k / \partial c$ as the gradient of `C` (and $\partial k / \partial T$ as the gradient of the expanded `T` with
`evolve_temperature`). The column of `C` for reaction $r$ receives the derivative of every output, so $k_r$ must depend
on `C[..., :, r]` (and `T[..., r]`) only: an evaluator that reads one column for all reactions puts every reaction's
derivative on that column, which the fall-off forms guard against by contracting over the species axis and keeping
the reaction axis ({{< code src/kinetics/troe_falloff.cpp TroeFalloffImpl::forward >}}). The forms at the pin add the
reaction axis to `T` when `T` and `P` have the same shape, so one module serves both calls. $k$ must be built from
differentiable torch operations; no hand-written derivative is read. Reactions named in `kf_override` get the supplied
value and a zero derivative.

*Mutation and ownership.* `C` and the expanded `T` are leaves that require gradients, so in-place operations on them are
refused by autograd; `P` and the tensors in `other` belong to the caller or are views of the module's own buffers
(`stoich`), and an evaluator must not modify them. Persistent state belongs in buffers registered in `reset`, which
`clone` reruns; nothing from one call should be kept for the next. Tensors that are not buffers do not follow `to`, and
must be moved at use, as the Arrhenius pressure switch does with
`p_threshold_.to(rate.device(), rate.scalar_type())`
({{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusImpl::switch_pressure >}}).

*dtype and device.* `Kinetics` registers the evaluator as a submodule, so `kinetics.to(device, dtype)` moves its
buffers. Tensors created inside `forward` should take the device and dtype of `T`, as the result tensor does. Torch
operations run on CPU and CUDA alike; a form that calls a scalar C function needs a CUDA version of it (@sec-ch12).

*Registration, five places in one order.* (1) An `ADD_ARG(XOptions, x)` member of `KineticsOptionsImpl`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsOptionsImpl >}}). (2) In `KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}), set the member from the
`reactions` list and call `add_to_vapor_cloud` for its species (@sec-ch02-species-registry). (3) Append it in
`KineticsOptionsImpl::reactions` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp KineticsOptionsImpl::reactions >}}). (4) In
`KineticsImpl::reset` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}}), give the member a default if it is
null, push the module onto the evaluator list, `register_module` it and push its reaction count, at the same position
as in step 3: the stoichiometry, the mass-action orders and the reverse columns are all built from `reactions()`, so a
different order assigns rate constants to the wrong reactions. (5) To build it from Python, bind the options class and
add the member to the `KineticsOptions` binding in `python/csrc/pykinetics.cpp`. The YAML `type` key is whatever
`from_yaml` selects on.

*Checks.* No kintera test exercises a hypothetical new form, but the existing ones are the pattern to copy: the value
against its closed form, called both with `(..., nspecies)` and with the per-reaction axis, as
`FalloffEndToEndTest.forward_three_body_distinguishes_species_and_reaction_axes` does; and $\partial k/\partial c$ from
`Kinetics.forward` against a central finite difference per reaction, relative tolerance $10^{-6}$, with the other
reactions' columns zero, as `test_rate_constant_ddC.py` does; on CPU and, where available, CUDA.

The band-selection figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| YAML reader | {{< code src/kinetics/arrhenius.cpp ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `from_yaml` | `rate-constant`[^rg-fe9f62b85a4d] |

: Code map of Arrhenius rate constants. {#tbl-ch06-arrhenius-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: `A_ranges` without `T_ranges`; band lists of different lengths; `T_ranges` not
strictly increasing; a reaction with no `type` or no `rate-constant`.

The key `E4` is parsed into `E4_R` but `forward` does not use it (verified by reading `forward` at the pin).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_multirange_arrhenius.py` | single band matches the closed form | $10^{-12}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_multirange_arrhenius_yaml.py` | YAML bands equal the Python API | $10^{-13}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_multirange_arrhenius_yaml.py` | inactive overflow stays out of $k$ | $2 \times 10^{-6}$ rel. | not yet derived |

: Tests of Arrhenius rate constants. {#tbl-ch06-arrhenius-tests}

The tolerances are read from the test files at the pin; the reason for each is missing evidence. No test covers the
`Ea_R` default or `E4`.

### Limits

`E4` is accepted and ignored. The `Ea_R` default is 1 K. Both are verified findings; whether they are intended is
an open question.

Evaluator contract: with `evolve_temperature`, `Kinetics` calls the backward pass of the evaluator's output
unconditionally, so a rate constant that depends on neither `T` nor `C` through autograd would raise an error there
(read from `forward_with_rate_constants`; not run, a hypothesis). The code at the pin does not determine whether an
evaluator may return a tensor on another device or dtype than `T` (the copy into the result would convert it; no form
does this), whether evaluators may be called from several threads, or any order other than the one in
`KineticsOptionsImpl::reactions`.
